channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Central Asian leaders pledge unity but actions lag behind rhetoric on cooperation
item.description: Leaders of six Central Asian nations and Azerbaijan met to discuss closer economic cooperation, trade, transport, and regional security. Turkmenistan expressed readiness to expand trade and digitalize economies, signaling a shift from its isolationist policies. President Berdymukhamedov called for a unified approach to key issues.

item.title: TRIPP project stalled by external factors, hindering Middle Corridor development
item.description: The Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project, intended to connect Azerbaijan to its exclave via Armenia, remains stalled over a year after its agreement. Principal obstacles are external, impeding the broader Middle Corridor initiative connecting Central Asia to Europe. The project aimed to integrate Armenia and Azerbaijan into this vital trade route.

item.title: Compensation Paid in Full to Families of Deceased Soldiers
item.description: Compensation has been fully paid to the families of deceased soldiers, according to Bekmurat Zhusipov, a member of the People's Council. Specific amounts and recipient details are not disclosed for security reasons. Payments were processed by a special commission with parental involvement.

item.title: Uzbekistan outlines priorities for its upcoming CIS chairmanship in 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the nation's priorities for its 2027 chairmanship of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). The focus will be on economy, new technologies, transport, security, education, and human capital development, under the motto "CIS - a space of trust and common development." Over one hundred specific measures are planned.

item.title: Kazakhstan strengthens ties with Europe, discussing counter-terrorism and diplomatic engagement
item.description: Kazakhstan participated in the second Central Asia-EU dialogue on counter-terrorism in Brussels. Kazakh diplomats also met with the new Irish Ambassador to Kazakhstan and attended a photo exhibition in Moldova. Discussions focused on current terrorist threats, strengthening international cooperation against terrorism and violent extremism, and exploring prospects for political, economic, and cultural exchange.

item.title: Ukraine Conflict Escalates, Russian Language Discussed, Nobel Peace Prize Awarded
item.description: The conflict in Ukraine intensifies with at least 70 deaths in the past two days. At a CIS summit, the President of Kazakhstan again addressed the issue of the Russian language. The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to a South African human rights defender.

item.title: Navanethem Pillay Awarded 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for Human Rights Advocacy
item.description: South African lawyer and human rights advocate Navanethem Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The 85-year-old was recognized for her efforts in promoting peace and strengthening legal mechanisms for human dignity and justice. Pillay previously served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014.

item.title: Kazakhstan Public Council Chairman Emphasizes Listening to Public Voice and Needs
item.description: Yerlan Koshanov, Chairman of the People's Council of Kazakhstan, met with representatives of public councils. He stressed the importance of establishing strong ties with regions through public councils, ensuring timely attention to public concerns and aspirations. The Council aims to consolidate diverse proposals from regions for national consideration.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ecological Party Discusses Green Development Principles with Youth
item.description: The Central Council of Uzbekistan's Ecological Party hosted an event on "Green Development Through the Eyes of Youth." The program included a book presentation on green development principles and an open dialogue about environmental reforms and youth's role. Officials emphasized the importance of environmental culture and youth engagement in the transition to green development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Mandating Public Reporting by Officials to Public Councils
item.description: Kazakhstan is proposing legislation to require heads of state bodies to personally report to public councils on their recommendations' implementation. This initiative aims to enhance accountability. Other proposed measures include sharing successful regional practices and developing inter-council cooperation to address common issues.

item.title: Seventeen Sentenced in Almaty for Involvement in Asar Baspana Financial Pyramid Scheme
item.description: Seventeen individuals have been sentenced in Almaty for their roles in the Asar Baspana financial pyramid scheme. The scheme allegedly defrauded approximately 90,000 citizens of 25 billion tenge by promising high monthly returns. Assets worth 5.6 billion tenge will be used to compensate victims, with remaining property to be confiscated by the state.

item.title: US State Department Report: Taliban and Other Groups Unlawfully Recruit Child Soldiers in Afghanistan
item.description: The US State Department's 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report states that the Taliban and other armed groups in Afghanistan unlawfully recruit and use children. Groups like ISIS-K and the NRF reportedly use child soldiers in combat and support roles, including planting explosives and guarding bases.

item.title: Akim Fined Over 430,000 Tenge for Issuing False Certificate in Akmola Region
item.description: A rural district Akim in the Akmola region was fined over 430,000 tenge for issuing a false certificate to an entrepreneur. The certificate, which contained inaccurate information, was used to gain an advantage in a land plot tender, violating the investor's rights. The prosecutor's office intervened to protect the investor's project.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Pursue Strategic Partnership Amidst Growing Trade
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are strengthening their relationship, moving towards a strategic partnership. Following a period of increased openness since 2016, leaders have engaged in regular meetings. Political trust forms the basis of their cooperation, with aligned approaches to regional security and non-interference. Trade turnover reached $1.14 billion in 2024, marking a 5.5% increase.

item.title: Azerbaijan's State Newspaper Highlights Mirziyoyev's Regional Cooperation Initiatives
item.description: Azerbaijan's official newspaper 'Azerbayjan' published an article on President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's initiatives for regional cooperation. The piece focuses on proposals to expand trade, develop joint production, and enhance transport links. It emphasizes Azerbaijan's role in connecting Central Asia and highlights potential for collaboration in trade, transport, energy, and technology.

item.title: Uzbek President Addresses CIS Heads of State Summit in Turkmenistan
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev thanked Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdymukhamedov for hosting the CIS summit in Avaza. Mirziyoyev congratulated attendees on the Commonwealth's 35th anniversary, noting the changing world but enduring human connections and cooperation potential. He emphasized strengthening trust and achieving real results through economic integration and industrial cooperation to boost trade and investment.

item.title: Desperate Afghans Sell Kidneys to Escape Debt and Hunger
item.description: Facing overwhelming debt and unable to feed their children, desperate Afghans are selling their kidneys on the black market. Zahira, a mother of two, sold one kidney last year, but it did not save her family from poverty and has negatively impacted her health. An estimated number of impoverished Afghans are selling organs, primarily kidneys, to survive amid the worsening humanitarian crisis since the Taliban takeover.

item.title: Aid distributed to families of deceased servicemen in Mangystau region
item.description: A commission has concluded its work in the Mangystau region, distributing financial aid to families of deceased and injured servicemen. Funds collected by the "Ұлттық рух" foundation have all been allocated. The aid distribution was carried out under the instruction of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

item.title: China tightens vehicle export rules, requiring service centers abroad from 2027
item.description: China will implement stricter vehicle and motorcycle export regulations starting in 2027. Exporters must establish overseas service centers, provide cooperation agreements, repair documentation, and proof of staff qualifications. Rules for re-equipped vehicles are also tightening, requiring official manufacturer approval.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Slowdown in Consumer Credit Growth, Regulator Reports
item.description: The growth of consumer credit portfolios in Kazakhstan slowed to 7.5% in August 2026, down from 14.6% in August 2025. The Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market attributed this to measures restricting unsecured lending, including stricter debt load requirements and limits on consumer loan amounts. The agency also reported a decrease in loans obtained fraudulently.

item.title: Commission Distributes Funds to Families of Military Personnel Lost at Sea
item.description: A commission has completed its work distributing financial aid to families of military personnel killed or injured during exercises in the Caspian Sea. Funds collected from enterprises, entrepreneurs, and patrons were allocated through a special fund. The commission, comprising law enforcement, public representatives, and deputies, ensured fair and equitable distribution according to legal procedures.

item.title: Mourning in Mangystau: Payments to Families of Deceased Soldiers Kept Confidential
item.description: In the Mangystau region, funds collected for families of soldiers who died during exercises have been distributed. However, the amounts of these payments will not be disclosed at the request of the relatives for security and confidentiality reasons. The regional public council chairman confirmed the commission's work is complete and all funds have been distributed according to law.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Addresses Caspian Ecological Summit in Turkmenistan
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev spoke at the Caspian Ecological Summit in Turkmenistan, calling the meeting historic. He emphasized the Caspian Sea's strategic importance as a natural resource, transport, and energy hub. Tokayev warned that the ecological situation is becoming an economic crisis, requiring urgent action to prevent irreparable damage.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Inflation Control Hindered by Currency-Centric Expectations, Study Finds
item.description: A report by AERC indicates that while tenge depreciation temporarily boosts inflation expectations in Kazakhstan, this effect is short-lived. Actual price increases do not significantly impact public forecasts. Analysts suggest this currency-centric and unanchored expectation structure complicates monetary policy and may reflect public distrust in official inflation data.

item.title: Almaty Launches 'People's Participation Budget' Project for Citizen Proposals
item.description: Almaty has opened applications for its 'People's Participation Budget' project, allowing residents to submit proposals for urban improvement until November 1, 2026. Selected initiatives, supported by public voting, will be implemented in 2027. Projects must be for public use, within district authority competence, and not commercially driven, with a maximum cost of 324.3 million tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes International Project Pool for Caspian Sea Rescue
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed consolidating international efforts and creating a pool of promising projects to save the Caspian Sea at an ecological summit. He emphasized the need to restore water flow, river deltas, and wetlands, and to establish a permanent secretariat for the Tehran Convention. Kazakhstan will continue efforts to create a UN-backed International Water Organization to improve global water resource management with a focus on the Caspian's environmental state.

item.title: Caspian Seal Population Decreased from One Million to 270,000
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated at the Caspian Ecological Summit that the Caspian seal population has declined from one million to 270,000 over the past century. He attributed this decline to sea shallowing, habitat changes, pollution, and anthropogenic pressure, calling for intensified joint efforts to protect vulnerable species and combat illegal fishing and trafficking.

item.title: Caspian Sea Lost Over 16,000 Square Kilometers in 25 Years, Says Tokayev
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced at the Caspian Ecological Summit that the Caspian Sea has lost over 16,000 square kilometers between 2000 and 2025 due to reduced water inflow, climate warming, and anthropogenic load. He warned of potential mass migration due to climate factors and threats to navigation, fishing, and coastal communities, highlighting the risk of an ecological catastrophe.

item.title: Section of Abylai Khan Avenue in Almaty to be Closed This Weekend for LRT Construction
item.description: A section of Abylai Khan Avenue in Almaty, between Raimbek Avenue and Mametova Street, will be completely closed to traffic from October 10th to October 11th due to Light Rail Transit (LRT) construction. Warning signs will be installed, and drivers are advised to plan their routes in advance. Bus and trolleybus routes will also be rerouted.

item.title: ADB Grants $1 Million for "Green" Energy Corridor Project Involving Uzbekistan
item.description: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) has allocated a $1 million grant for the initial phase of the "Caspian Green Energy Corridor" project. This project aims to connect the energy systems of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Azerbaijan. The grant will fund the feasibility study for a subsea cable between Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan, with Uzbekistan connecting via land networks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Over 100 Events During CIS Presidency
item.description: During its upcoming presidency of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Uzbekistan plans to implement over 100 events. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized focusing on practical results, removing trade barriers, utilizing Central Asia's transport potential, and strengthening scientific ties. The presidency's concept and action plan are nearing completion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Lawmakers Debate Punishment for Sexual Abuse of Minors Amid Public Outcry
item.description: Following public testimonies of sexual abuse, Kyrgyzstani lawmakers are debating penalties for those convicted of sexual offenses against minors. Numerous citizens have shared their experiences of abuse on social media, highlighting a systemic issue that has prompted parliamentary discussion on stricter legal measures.

item.title: Fergana Oil Refinery Not Slated for Reprivatization, State Assets Agency Reports
item.description: The State Assets Management Agency announced that the Fergana Oil Refinery is not currently scheduled for reprivatization. The agency's director, Sohibjon Murodov, stated that the company's debts are being reviewed as part of an international audit. Production volumes have increased significantly, with diesel fuel output up 30% and aviation fuel production multiplied several times.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explains Privatization Terms for 'Uzekspomarkaz' and International Cooperation Center
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Assets Management Agency Director explained the specific privatization terms for 'Uzekspomarkaz' and the International Cooperation Center. These entities, located in green zones of Tashkent, will be privatized under special conditions agreed upon with the Presidential Administration, aligning with the 'Green Zone' state program.

item.title: CIS Adopts Tajikistan's Proposal to Form a Positive Image of the Commonwealth
item.description: The CIS Heads of State adopted measures to create a positive image of the organization and its member states in the information space. Initiated by Tajikistan, the decision aims to develop coordinated approaches to prevent actions that could harm the reputation of the CIS and its participants, promoting responsible information policies.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Urges Regional Support for Afghanistan's Stability
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov called on regional nations to maintain support for Afghanistan, emphasizing that a stable country benefits the entire region. Speaking at a Central Asian leaders' meeting, he stressed the need for continued humanitarian aid and enhanced cooperation against terrorism, drug trafficking, and organized crime. Upholding commitments to Afghanistan is crucial for regional security.

item.title: UK Sanctions Third Kyrgyz Finance Ministry Company for Aiding Russia
item.description: The UK has imposed sanctions on Processing KG, a company affiliated with Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Finance. This marks the third such company to be sanctioned for allegedly assisting Russia. The sanctions highlight international pressure on entities perceived to be supporting Russia's economic activities.

item.title: Turkmenistan Imposes Strict Quarantine Measures at Border Crossing Amid Suspected Pneumonia Outbreak in Russia
item.description: Turkmenistan has reinstated strict COVID-19-like quarantine measures at the Garabogaz border crossing with Kazakhstan. Unconfirmed sources suggest this is due to a suspected pneumonia outbreak in Russia. Health officials are reportedly disinfecting the area and passengers, with some travelers being placed in quarantine.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Chair CIS Summit in Bukhara in 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan will chair the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) in 2027, with the CIS summit scheduled to be held in Bukhara on October 8-9. Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan will co-chair alongside Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlined priorities including economy, new technologies, transport, security, education, science, and human potential development.

item.title: First Caspian Ecological Summit Held in Turkmenistan's Avaza National Tourist Zone
item.description: The First Caspian Ecological Summit convened in Turkmenistan's Avaza National Tourist Zone on October 9, 2026. Presidents from Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, and Russia participated. The summit focused on environmental protection and preserving the Caspian Sea's ecosystem, resulting in a heads of state decision. Turkmenistan advocates for cooperation within the UN framework for sustainable development and marine environment protection.
